event.title: <show-title>Mysterious Skin (4K Restoration)</show-title><event-type-title> with Live Q&A</event-type-title>
event.headline: Director     Gregg Araki Live in Person
event.description:
In-person Q&A with filmmaker Gregg Araki following the screening.

At the age of eight, Kansas youngsters Neil and Brian played on the same little league baseball team. Now, ten years later, the two boys couldn't be more different. Neil is a charismatic but emotionally aloof male hustler, while Brian is a nervous introvert obsessed with the idea that he has been abducted by a UFO. When the boy's parallel lives inevitably intersect, the pair unearth dark, repressed secrets on a harrowing and unforgettable journey of self-discovery.

A statement from Gregg Araki: "I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it."

Digitally restored by the Academy Film Archive and UCLA Film & Television Archive in conjunction with Sundance Institute in 4K from the original 35 mm A/B camera negatives and original sound elements. The restoration was supervised by Gregg Araki at Resillion and Monkeyland Audio. The restoration was funded by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, mk2, Frameline, Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive, with additional funding and services by Antidote Films and Strand Releasing.

  • Washington, DC: Editor/producer Scott Evans.
  • San Antonio at Park North: Cast members David Elizondo, Quinn Matthews, and journalist Stephanie Koithan (San Antonio Current)

show.headline: A Swedish splatterpunk satire on the making of a horror movie!

event.title: <show-title>Evil Ed</show-title>
event.headline: A Swedish splatterpunk satire on the making of a horror movie!
event.description: Part of cinema’s “moviemaking” meta-horror lineage alongside BERBERIAN SOUND STUDIO and WES CRAVEN’S NEW NIGHTMARE, EVIL ED is gross and shocking in all the right places. Film editor Eddie is transferred by his boss to their studio's “Splatter and Gore” department. There, Eddie is to cut the more offensive scenes out of the company's LOOSE LIMBS horror series so that they can be marketed to foreign countries. At first, Eddie goes about his task as he would any other assignment. But viewing all the blood-spattered footage takes its toll…Eddie hallucinates that his food is dismembered body parts, and he sees demons living in his fridge! A rare splatter film from Sweden, EVIL ED rises from the VHS ashes in a beautiful restoration.

show.title: Ringu
show.headline: The J-Horror classic returns to theaters with a new restoration

event.title: <show-title>Ringu</show-title>
event.headline: The J-Horror classic returns to theaters in a new restoration.
event.description:
Television journalist Reiko investigates an urban legend about a cursed VHS tape that murders the viewer seven days after they watch it. As the mystery hits closer to home, Reiko joins forces with ex-husband/current-exorcist Takashi to destroy the curse. And (hopefully) survive an encounter with a ghost named Sadako. Directed by Hideo Nakata (DARK WATER), RINGU is the highest grossing Japanese horror movie in history that STILL manages to shred our nerves with its quiet, phantasmic elegance. This is the only VHS fetish movie in history to inspire an entire subgenre, as well as dozens of remakes and rip-offs. Criminally absent from theaters since its original theatrical release in 1998, the time is now for RINGU to terrify the world. Again.

Restoration courtesy of Arrow Films and the American Genre Film Archive.

event.headline: Beyond the horizon lies the secret to a new beginning.
event.description:
The most expensive film ever made at the time of its release, Waterworld has thrilled audiences through the years with its awe-inspiring action scenes, gargantuan maritime sets and ground-breaking special effects.

A definitive post-apocalypse blockbuster, Waterworld stars Kevin Costner (THE UNTOUCHABLES) as The Mariner - a mutant trader, adrift in a dystopian future where Earth is submerged under water and humankind struggles to survive on boats and in ramshackle floating cities. The Mariner becomes embroiled with the Smokers, a gang of pirates who, led by villainous leader Deacon (Dennis Hopper, BLUE VELVET), are seeking Enola (Tina Majorino, NAPOLEON DYNAMITE), a girl with a map to the mythical realm of Dryland tattooed on her back. (Arrow Video)

event.title: <show-title>Little Shop of Horrors (1986)</show-title>
event.headline: Oz, Ashman, and Menken’s iconically queer monster movie musical turns 40!
event.description:
Feed me, Seymour. Feed me all night long.

Alarm goes off at seven, and you start uptown. You put in your eight hours for the powers that have always been. Ugh, ain’t that the truth, Chiffon?

It’s been a hot minute since we’ve screened a musical for Queer Film Theory 101, so in honor of its 40th anniversary, we’re showing the melodic and incendiary critique of hustle culture, LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS, from powerhouse writing duo Howard Ashman and Alan Menken and director Frank Oz. Well ahead of its time, this film tackles hot topics like urban decay, abusive dentistry, aggressively sexual plants, and presages the rise of influencer culture.

When dopey orphan-turned-beleaguered florist’s assistant Seymour (Rick Moranis) stumbles upon an exceptionally strange and exotic plant, he suddenly sees a way out of Skid Row for himself and the equally troubled object of his affection, Audrey (Ellen Green). Unfortunately for everyone involved, Seymour’s leafy meal ticket, Audrey II (Levi Stubbs), harbors murderous desires of its own, revealing itself as an extraterrestrial invader hell-bent on human domination.

Featuring an all-star cast including Steve Martin, John Candy, Tisha Campbell, and Bill Murray, unforgettable songs from Ashman and Menken, and incredible puppetry from Lyle Conway (THE DARK CRYSTAL, The Muppet Show), LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS is perhaps the perfect movie musical. Don’t argue with us. Deeply queer, filled with critiques of capitalism, and catchy as hell, we can’t wait to celebrate this iconic musical's 40th anniversary with y’all as part of Queer Film Theory 101. And just a gentle reminder: don’t feed the plants!

show.title: The Piano
show.headline: A tale of lust and seduction

event.title: <show-title>The Piano</show-title>
event.headline: Holly Hunter’s ultimate mute sad girl performance won her a much deserved Oscar
event.description:
THE PIANO centers on a mute Scottish woman, Ada McGrath (Holly Hunter), who is shipped off to rural New Zealand to marry settler Alisdair Stewart (Sam Neill). She travels with the two most important things in her life: her out-of-wedlock daughter (Anna Paquin) and the ornate piano she uses to express her feelings through. When her new husband sells her piano to a frontiersman (Harvey Keitel), Ada finds herself in an unexpected affair that leads to dark consequences.

THE PIANO earned three Academy Awards: one for Hunter, one for Paquin, and one for Jane Campion (THE POWER OF THE DOG) for best screenplay. A gentle but sometimes harsh film, THE PIANO is a stunning, complex romance not unlike WUTHERING HEIGHTS. It feels deeply rooted in its time period and organic in its storytelling. Keitel and Hunter’s chemistry is lightning – a smouldering sensation that radiates through the screen. The romance Campion directs is profoundly messy, and because of that messiness, it’s profoundly beautiful.

show.title: Michael Mann's Manhunter: The Final Cut
show.headline: New 4K restoration of Michael Mann's final cut

event.title: <show-title>Michael Mann's Manhunter: The Final Cut</show-title>
event.headline: New 4K restoration of Michael Mann's final cut
event.description:
A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert – the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris' four novels featuring the iconic murderer Lecktor, and benefits from the filmmaker's typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast, including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen as his blind love interest.

This new 4K final cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version. Shot in 1985, MANHUNTER was on a frontier in both its subject matter and film form, initiating an impressive list of subsequent films and series. (Rialto)

show.headline: A twisted horror comedy from the director of BARBERSHOP

event.title: <show-title>The Blackening</show-title>
event.headline: A twisted horror comedy from the director of BARBERSHOP.
event.description: THE BLACKENING centers around a group of Black friends who reunite for a Juneteenth weekend getaway only to find themselves trapped in a remote cabin with a twisted killer. Forced to play by his rules, the friends soon realize this ain’t no motherf****** game. Directed by Tim Story (RIDE ALONG, BARBERSHOP) and co-written by Tracy Oliver (GIRLS TRIP) and Dewayne Perkins (The Amber Ruffin Show), THE BLACKENING skewers genre tropes and delivers a bloody-good time for anyone who likes belly laughs with their dismemberment.

show.headline: Fedoras! Disco Mutants! Atomic Punks!

event.title: <show-title>Radioactive Dreams</show-title>
event.headline: Albert Pyun’s hard-boiled post-apocalyptic musical action comedy!
event.description:
Albert Pyun doesn’t blend genres so much as drop an absolute A-Bomb on them in this riotous adventure. Philip and Marlowe emerge from their fallout shelter with dreams of being private eyes, just like they’d read about growing up. But will the wasteland change these wide-eyed pals when they step into a world of mutants, cannibals, red-wigged biker women, foul-mouthed child gangsters, enormous mutated sewer monsters and nuclear MacGuffins? Absolutely crammed with car chases, gun battles, fog machines and goofy Eighties fun, you’ll want the world to end just so you can dance your blues away doing the Post-Nuke Shuffle.

35mm print courtesy of the University of North Carolina School of the Arts

marketStrings.value: The personal closed captioning device displays feature film dialogue and other audio in the form of English-language text for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.

The descriptive audio headset provides individuals who are blind or have low vision with an English-language narration of the details of the feature presentation that can't be understood by the soundtrack alone.

Upon request at the box office, we provide assistive listening headsets with amplified audio for those individuals who are hard of hearing. For guests who prefer to use their own hearing aids, neck loops, or cochlear implants, our assistive listening headsets have a 3.5mm headphone jack to connect to those devices.

In order to ensure the highest quality experience for all guests, you may not enter a movie after it has started. We’d love to see you up to 30 minutes early. Running late? No worries, we will happily exchange your ticket for a different showtime or a raincheck to a future show.
